layout_summary: A two-column poster: a glossy red stiletto bleeds in from the left edge, its heel melting into a pitchfork-shaped drip that stabs into a Biscoff jar in the lower-left; the right column holds a stacked movie-title-style serif headline set at mid-height. A single centred line of rounded bold red copy sits across the bottom as a sign-off.

The heel drip, the pitchfork and the jar share one vertical axis at x≈24%

scene.subject: A high-gloss lacquered red stiletto pump in profile, toe cropped off the left edge. Its stiletto heel melts into a thin red liquid stream that ends in a three-pronged pitchfork; the pitchfork tips turn into caramel-brown spread and plunge into the open top of a glass jar of smooth caramelised biscuit spread with a red label. Thick spread overflows the rim and runs down the sides and over the label, pooling at the base. A biscuit is pressed against the side of the jar.
scene.composition: The shoe runs diagonally from the lower-left edge (x=0, y≈52%) up to its heel cup at x≈36%, y≈10%. The heel drip falls vertically at x≈24% from y≈34% to y≈48%, where the pitchfork spans x≈21.5–28%, y≈48–55%. The jar sits at x≈14.5–35%, y≈56–82.5% with its centre on the drip axis. The shoe is cropped at the left edge, and the jar is complete.
scene.camera: Straight-on side view at about jar height for the jar, pure profile for the shoe. Long-lens product feel with little perspective distortion and everything sharp.
scene.lighting: Soft studio key from upper left with crisp specular highlights on the patent shoe and glossy spread, plus a faint soft contact shadow under the jar. Clean neutral white.

ornaments.description: Thin black arrow that forms the right stroke of the V in DEVIL and continues up and to the right past the cap line, ending in a small arrowhead (a devil-tail/pitchfork nod), stroke weight matching the serif hairline-to-stem

why_it_works: Recognising a borrowed film title does the work in about a second: one swapped word ('Wears' → 'Eats') plus the red stiletto makes the parody instant, and the product is the punchline.
The image holds up without the headline: a heel melting into a devil's pitchfork that stabs the jar reads as 'devilish temptation' with no words at all.

There is strict figure/ground on pure white: the only saturated mass is the red shoe and the caramel jar, while the type stays black with small red accents. A large calm right-hand quadrant and a 10% bottom band give the eye a clean path: shoe → jar → title → sign-off line.
